title: TurfBot: stateless PKCE in Flask
subtitle: Signed state instead of server-side login storage, and a role-filtered service account
summary: TurfBot implements the same PKCE sign-in by hand in Flask. The code verifier and nonce travel inside an itsdangerous-signed, ten-minute state parameter, so nothing is stored between /login and /callback. The ID token is verified against Keycloak's JWKS, and the realm roles decide which tools Claude may use.

sections.title: Signed state
Callback: exchange and verify
Security points
items: Tampered or expired state is refused before any token request is made.
safe_next() only accepts same-site relative paths: no open redirect after sign-in.
The tools call the APIs as svc-chatbot (SVC_READ); the user's roles are enforced in TurfBot twice: when binding tools to Claude and again in the tools node.
Sign-out calls Keycloak's end-session endpoint with id_token_hint, ending SSO for every module.
